mechanism_narrative: The rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-1w to t-0w signals renewed daytime activity that should spill into retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks versus the prior four.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain near t-0w levels but RETAIL_REC does not rise above the last-4-week mean within 4 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL time above 25 percent above baseline reflects stay-at-home behavior that suppresses discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 25 and stays above that level for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 27.1 at t-1w before easing to 20.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 25 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior two-week average within the next 2 weeks, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover sharply from one week to the next, the city is likely moving into a looser access regime that supports broader retail footfall and raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises at least 8 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES rises at least 8 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If a week-on-week gain of at least 8 points in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is followed by no increase in RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in GROCERY_PHARM indicates restored essential-trip mobility and neighborhood circulation, which should modestly pull RETAIL_REC upward within one week through nearby errand bundling.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises for a full week but RETAIL_REC does not move upward in the same week or the next week, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in PARKS and TRANSIT indicates fewer discretionary outings overall, which should depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as outing intensity falls.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15 while TRANSIT remains below -55
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -21.1 to -9.3 while TRANSIT stayed deeply negative
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below -15 and TRANSIT below -55 but RETAIL_REC does not decline versus the last-2-week mean within 2 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility continues to recover while RESIDENTIAL softens, weekend substitution into outdoor activity should ease and retail visits should rise over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases for 2 consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL declines for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS rises for two weeks and RESIDENTIAL falls for two weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous jump in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and RETAIL_REC after a trough indicates easing movement constraints; under that regime, retail mobility should remain above the recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rebound by more than 10 points from a local low
failure_condition: If large rebounds in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not coincide with a sustained increase in RETAIL_REC over the following 4 weeks, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: The recent rise in GROCERY_PHARM combined with the easing of RESIDENTIAL time suggests more routine errand-based activity and less home confinement, which should lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -10.1 to -4.9 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 27.1 to 20.9
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL falls but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.
